facts.says: Varrock is the capital of Misthalin and the biggest city most people will ever see.
The city began as a camp called Avarrocka, pitched by a tribe who found the boy Arrav and took him for a good omen.
The museum calls Arrav the best-known hero of the Fourth Age, and there are plenty of legends about him.
King Roald rules Misthalin from Varrock Palace, and Queen Ellamaria lives there with him.
Some townsfolk grumble that the king isn't much good and that they could do with a new one.
King Roald rebuilt a ruin in the north-west that people called Ghost Town and renamed it Edgeville.
The palace is the largest building in the city, with barracks for the guard, kitchens, a library and the Queen's garden.
A grizzly bear is kept in a cage in the north-east corner of the palace grounds.
Guards stand at every gate into Varrock and keep quarters along the city walls.
The city loses guards so quickly that even their sergeant can't keep track of the new faces.
Captain Rovin heads the palace guard, takes his job very seriously, and will only take orders from the king.
There's a pillory behind the general store where wrongdoers are locked up.
Muggers and thieves work Varrock's streets, and one thief loiters watching the fancy house by the south gate.
Dark wizards hang about the stone circle just south of the city, on the road to Lumbridge, and set on weaker travellers.
The Wilderness starts not far north of the city, just beyond Edgeville's ditch, which is why so many armed adventurers pass through.
Varrock Square in the middle of town is where most of the shops are, with five stalls in the square itself.
Baraek runs the fur stall in the square, and he'll only haggle so far because he has a family to feed.
Benny sells the Varrock Herald in the square for fifty coins and promises interviews and scandal in every edition.
The tea stall south-east of the east bank sells a cup for ten coins, and the seller shouts if you touch the cups on display.
Horvik sells platebodies and chainmail, Lowe sells bows and arrows, Zaff sells staves, and the swordshop sells daggers and swords.
Thessalia's shop sells robes, capes, gloves and boots, and she'll change how you're dressed for nothing.
Emma runs the hair salon north of the museum, with her shy sister Suzie and their parrot Rio.
The apothecary in the south-west of the city mixes strength and energy potions if you bring him what he needs.
Aubury keeps the rune shop near the east bank and sells most sorts of rune, chaos and death runes included.
The Grand Exchange, just north-west of the palace, is where the whole world comes to buy and sell, and it's the busiest place there is.
The museum east of the palace keeps the history of Gielinor, run by the curator Haig Halen, with a historian who swaps rewards for adventurers' stories.
The museum tells how seven priestly warriors drove evil back into Morytania and Saradomin blessed the River Salve to keep it there.
Saradomin's church in the north-east of the city is draughty and shabby, and the two regulars sleep through in the pews.
Father Lawrence, the priest at the church, is a religious man and a regular drinker.
Old Elsie knits upstairs in the church, and for a cup of tea she'll tell how the Wise Old Man, as a young lad, daubed Saradominist boasts on the Zamorakian chapel.
Under the city are big sewers, reached by a manhole east of the palace, full of rats and moss giants, with a giant rat king called Scurrius.
The Champions' Guild south of the city only lets in adventurers who've made a name for themselves, and sells rune armour upstairs.
Among the hens in the Champions' Guild yard lives a very nasty chicken.
The Cooks' Guild just west of the city is only for proper cooks, and it has its own pie shop.
The Blue Moon Inn is the city's favourite pub; the Jolly Boar sits outside the walls to the north-east, and hardly anyone knows the Dancing Donkey.
Aris is an old fortune-teller with a tent by the square who will read your future for a coin.
Ask Aris her age and she tells you to count the stool legs in the Blue Moon Inn and multiply by seven.
About a hundred and fifty years ago a hero called Wally beat the demon Delrith with the sword Silverlight and sealed him in the stone circle.
Sir Prysin, one of the king's knights at the palace, is Wally's great-grandson.
Lumbridge, down the road to the south, is where fresh new adventurers turn up, and it's named for its bridge over the River Lum.
Falador, the White Knights' city and capital of Asgarnia, is a big place, though a little smaller than Varrock.
A museum display says the White Knights took over Falador when its old king fell ill, and they have been at war with the Black Knights ever since.
Charlie the Tramp hangs about the city asking passers-by for spare change.
Gertrude, a busy mother with four sons and a lot of cats, lives just west of the city, south of the Cooks' Guild.
Juliet lives in the Leptoc mansion just outside the western wall, by the west bank, and often stands on its balcony.
Romeo looks rather dense and soppy, wanders all over town, and will start talking to strangers without being asked.
Romeo is desperately in love with Juliet and hangs about the square pining for her.
Juliet's father, Draul Leptoc, an angry-looking lord, won't hear of her marrying Romeo.
Juliet drank a potion from the apothecary to look dead, so that Romeo could fetch her from the crypt.
In the crypt Romeo fell for Juliet's cousin Phillipa instead, still thinks Juliet is dead, and Juliet is thoroughly fed up with him.
Aris has foreseen that dark wizards are summoning the demon Delrith again, at the stone circle south of the city.
Sir Prysin keeps Silverlight locked in a box that needs three keys, one his, one Captain Rovin's and one held by a wizard.
An adventurer took up Silverlight, beat the demon Delrith at the stone circle and sealed him away again.
The museum's copy of Silverlight now has a card saying the sword was recently used to drive off Delrith once more.
Gertrude has lost her cat Fluffs and wants someone to find her.
Gertrude's boys Shilop and Wilough, who play about the square, were the last to see Fluffs, and they want paying before they'll say where.
Fluffs turned up in the Lumber Yard north-east of the city with a kitten, and both went home to Gertrude.
Gertrude now has kittens to spare, and sells them to people who'll raise them.
The necromancer Zemouregal raised Arrav, Avarrocka's old hero, from the dead and keeps him as his servant.
An adventurer broke into Zemouregal's vault, fought off Arrav himself, and got away with Arrav's heart, still beating.
Even with his heart back, Arrav isn't free of the necromancer yet, and the explorer Elias White is still looking for a way.
Varlamore, the Shining Kingdom far across the western sea, is ruled by a Sun Queen, and its people worship the sun and the moon.
Some bards passing through stayed a night at the Blue Moon Inn and talked for hours about Varlamore.
A delegation from Varlamore is due at the palace to sign a treaty with King Roald, and the square is waiting to see them.
Varlamore has kept itself shut off for hundreds of years, letting hardly anyone in or out, and is only now opening for travel and trade.
Alina in the square can't wait to visit Varlamore, while her friend Noah reckons it sounds like a prison and means to stay put.
Four bandits dressed as city guards were caught in the square before they could attack the Varlamore delegation.
The bandits had been paid to kill Servius, the Varlamore high priest, by someone who didn't look local.
Prince Itzla of Varlamore got bored of the talks and questioned one of the bandits himself, in the cell on the palace roof.
